what_it_does: This paper presents an analog-to-digital converter (ADC)—a chip component that captures radio signals and converts them to digital numbers for processing—running at 12 billion samples per second. These ultra-fast converters are essential for 5G wireless systems and radar arrays. The challenge is achieving both high sample rate and clean signal quality (low noise) using simple, area-efficient designs. This work uses 16 parallel conversion channels that take turns grabbing samples, each running slower but together achieving the full 12 gigasamples-per-second rate. The design uses a successive-approximation approach: each channel makes a quick binary guess about each signal bit, testing and refining until it converges to the right value.
